Pointwise convergence polynomials does* not* ensure uniform convergence.

Counterexample: B_n(x) = x^n, [0,1]. Pointwise limit f: f(x) = 0 ∀ x < 1, f(1) = 1. f discontinuous, x = 1. Uniform limits continuous functions necessarily continuous; discontinuous f precludes uniform convergence.

Qualification: continuous f restores uniformity. f ∈ C[0,1] ⟹ Banach–Steinhaus (Uniform Boundedness) theorem enforces uniform convergence.

Sketch: polynomials ⊂ C[0,1] (Banach, ‖·‖_∞). Evaluation functionals L_x(g) = g(x), ‖L_x‖ = 1 ∀ x. Pointwise convergence: L_x(B_n) → L_x(f) ∀ x. Banach–Steinhaus: pointwise boundedness {L_x(B_n)}_n ⟹ uniform boundedness. Tails: ‖B_n − f‖_∞ → 0 ⟹ uniform convergence.

Verdict: unrestricted pointwise convergence ⟹ no* uniformity. Continuous f ⟹ uniformity.
